description: Terrorist attacks on New York and Washington; US stock markets stay closed until 17 September.
US-led coalition begins the invasion of Iraq.
BNP Paribas suspends three funds exposed to US subprime mortgages; usually dated as the start of the global credit crunch.
JPMorgan Chase agrees to buy Bear Stearns with Federal Reserve backing.
Lehman Brothers files for the largest bankruptcy in US history.
Federal Reserve announces large-scale purchases of agency debt and mortgage-backed securities.
Euro area and IMF agree the first bailout package for Greece.
Federal Reserve announces 600 billion USD of additional Treasury purchases.
Standard & Poor's cuts the US sovereign rating from AAA to AA+ after the debt-ceiling standoff.
Swiss National Bank sets a minimum exchange rate of 1.20 francs per euro.
Federal Reserve begins open-ended mortgage-backed securities purchases.
Gold has its largest one-day fall in about 30 years after a sell-off that began on 12 April.
Ben Bernanke tells Congress the Fed could slow its bond purchases; yields jump.
Russia signs a treaty annexing Crimea from Ukraine.
Swiss National Bank removes the 1.20 franc-per-euro floor without warning.
People's Bank of China cuts the yuan's reference rate by about 2 percent.
UK votes to leave the European Union; the result is known on 24 June.
Donald Trump wins the US presidential election.
President Trump signs a memorandum directing tariffs on Chinese imports under Section 301.
China lets the yuan weaken past 7 per dollar; the US labels China a currency manipulator.
US drone strike in Baghdad kills Iranian general Qasem Soleimani.
World Health Organization characterises COVID-19 as a pandemic.

event_name: Fed cuts to zero and restarts QE
description: Emergency Sunday cut to 0-0.25 percent plus at least 700 billion USD of asset purchases.
The May WTI futures contract settles at about minus 37 USD per barrel.
Pfizer and BioNTech report over 90 percent efficacy; risk assets rally and gold falls.
Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Western allies announce sanctions freezing the Bank of Russia's foreign reserves; often cited as a reason for record central-bank gold buying.
Silicon Valley Bank is closed by regulators after a deposit run.
UBS agrees to take over Credit Suisse in a deal arranged by Swiss authorities.
Hamas-led attack on Israel begins the Gaza war.

event_name: Iran's first direct attack on Israel
description: Iran launches drones and missiles at Israel.
Donald Trump wins the US presidential election.
US announces broad reciprocal tariffs on most trading partners.
US pauses most reciprocal tariffs for 90 days while raising tariffs on China.
Israel attacks Iranian nuclear and military sites; start of the twelve-day war.
US bombs the Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan nuclear facilities.
Kevin Warsh is announced as the next Fed chair; the dollar jumps and gold has one of its largest one-day falls on record, a day after an all-time high.
US and Israeli strikes on Iran begin the 2026 Iran war.
Tanker traffic through Hormuz stops and QatarEnergy halts gas output; the IEA calls it the largest oil supply disruption on record.
Iran and the United States announce a ceasefire; Hormuz traffic stays well below pre-war levels.

event_name: Fed hikes for the first time since 2023
description: FOMC raises the target range by 25 bp to 3.75-4.00 percent to fight energy-driven inflation.
Drone strike on the tanker MT Petro Dolphin is followed by attacks on at least 15 vessels; Brent climbs back above 110 USD.
